keyboard.action: Activates the control when it renders as a button. An anchor activates on Enter only.

notes: Native button or anchor, so role, focus order and activation come from the element — do not add role="button".
An icon-only button needs an accessible name from the label prop; the icon is decorative and must not be the only name.
disabled is a real attribute on the button form, not a class. An anchor cannot be disabled — remove href instead.

decisions.question: href, state, onClick exist in the component but have no design counterpart. Confirm each is authored (lever true) or integration-only (lever false). "state" collides with the State axis, which this draft read as runtime states — decide whether the code prop or the state axis is the truth.
decisions.chose: added 3 code-only props as levers with no design binding
decisions.fix: Set lever:false on the integration-only ones, or delete any the component should stop accepting.

decisions.question: icon-start, icon-end have no class of their own in button.css — they all share .c-button__icon. The design names these parts separately and the code does not. Split the class, or model them as one part.
decisions.fix: Set anatomy.root.parts.<part>.selector to the real class, or add the class to button.css.

decisions.question: Scaffolded as card (default when no stronger signal is present). Confirm, or re-run npm run specs:scaffold -- --slug=button --archetype=<link-card|card|collection>.
alternatives: link-card: A card that is one link: illustration or icon, a headline, optional description, an arrow affordance. The whole surface is the target and the headline is the accessible name.
collection: A row, grid or scroller of one repeated unit.
decisions.evidence: roles media, eyebrow, icon; pattern n/a
decisions.decision: Button, not card. The scaffold fell back to card because no signal was stronger, and that default propagated: the contract declared its root element as article and described itself as a non-interactive content card. button.js settles it — createButton does document.createElement(href ? 'a' : 'button') and decorateButton decorates an existing anchor or button. "button" is in upstream's closed archetype enum, so it emits.
